profile.name: Jev for computer use
profile.description: Automates the web with TypeSafe Jev on a Chrome you can watch. Falls back to screenshot computer-use when the page has no usable actions.

memory.content: This bot’s job is web automation with TypeSafe Jev on the Chrome the user can see, not a hidden display. Screenshot computer-use is the fallback when the action list is empty, the page is a bot wall, or the loop will not end.

Needs a TypeSafe API key in secrets or .env, a small TYPE_TEXT helper, and BU_CDP_URL pointed at the visible Chrome’s remote-debugging port. Never invent ports or keys; never send, post, buy, or pay without an explicit yes.

Visibility rules: drive only the visible Chrome; activate the target tab before acting; prefer reuse over background tabs; judge success on the live URL/title/text; screenshot after real milestones for proof; clear leftover search/UI between tasks.

skills.name: jev-browser-computer-use
skills.description: Use when a Grok Bot should automate the web with TypeSafe Jev on the box Chrome desktop instead of screenshot computer-use.
skills.content:
---
name: jev-browser-computer-use
description: >-
  Use when a Grok Bot should automate the web with TypeSafe Jev on the box
  Chrome desktop instead of screenshot computer-use.
---
Goal: run web tasks on this bot’s Chrome with TypeSafe Jev. Jev picks from the page’s accessibility or DOM action list. You own the VM, CDP, and a small TYPE_TEXT helper. This is not a screenshot-vision click loop.

Use this when the site has usable links, forms, search, or list rows; you want a timed compare against screenshot computer-use; or the user should see the same Chrome you drive.

Skip this when the site shows a bot wall, blank title, or empty action list, or the work is outside the browser. Then use ordinary screenshot computer-use.

Setup (once): clone jev-ultrafast and run uv sync; turn on remote debugging for the Chrome on the desktop the user watches and note that CDP URL; put TYPESAFE_API_KEY in secrets or .env (never print it); set TYPESAFE_MODEL to the current Jev model id; point TEXT_MODEL_* at a small helper that only answers TYPE_TEXT prompts; set BU_CDP_URL to that visible Chrome, not another display’s Chrome.

Visibility: drive only the Chrome the user can see; activate that tab before you act and reuse it — do not hide work in a background tab and call it done; judge success on the live page (URL, title, visible text), not on a finished log line; screenshot after real milestones and when you report a result (skip per-click shots — screenshots prove what happened, they are not the main control loop while Jev has a good action list); if the user is watching, pause long enough on each page or open one tab per stop; clear stuck search boxes and dialogs between tasks; free-form typing goes through the TYPE_TEXT helper.

Run: confirm the visible Chrome and BU_CDP_URL; start the text helper if you need TYPE_TEXT; activate the tab, navigate or reuse it; run jev-ultrafast with a step or time budget; check the live page and screenshot when you report; if actions are empty, the same click repeats, or the loop will not end, stop, screenshot, then change approach or fall back to screenshot computer-use.

Do not invent ports, keys, or passwords; do not send, post, buy, or pay without a clear yes; do not treat a hidden-window CDP success as something the user saw; do not swap Jev out for a chat model on every click when the action list is fine.

Timed compares: start the clock after the first ready page; stop at verified success; save steps, wall time, and a short outcome JSON.

skills.name: jev-ultrafast-cursor
skills.description: Use when a local Cursor agent should drive the browser with TypeSafe Jev / jev-ultrafast instead of screenshot computer-use.
skills.content:
---
name: jev-ultrafast-cursor
description: >-
  Use when a local Cursor agent should drive the browser with TypeSafe Jev /
  jev-ultrafast instead of screenshot computer-use.
---
Goal: drive the browser with jev-ultrafast. TypeSafe Jev picks an operation and element index from a live action table. A small text model fills TYPE_TEXT only. Prefer this over screenshot clicking when the page exposes real controls and you are on the browser the operator can see.

Use this when: structured sites (search, flights, forms, Wikipedia, HN, docs); speed checks against screenshot computer-use; the user asks for Jev, TypeSafe, or indexed browser actions.

Skip this when: bot walls, empty titles, or empty action tables; work outside the browser.

How it fits together: the page builds an indexed element table; Jev picks operation plus index; TYPE_TEXT calls a small model; Browser Harness or CDP runs the action. One plain-language goal. Targets are indexes, not CSS selectors or generated code. DONE is not success — check the live page.

Visibility: point CDP at the Chrome the user is watching; activate that tab and prefer reuse over background tabs; screenshot that window after real steps and when you report; on empty actions, blocks, or loops, stop, screenshot, then fall back to screenshot computer-use; for watchable tours, pause or use separate tabs; clear leftover UI between tasks; do not invent ports or keys; do not send or pay without a yes.

Setup: clone jev-ultrafast, uv sync, copy .env.example to .env. Set TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_MODEL, TEXT_MODEL_* for typing, and BU_CDP_URL to the visible Chrome. Use Browser Harness doctor if Chrome will not connect.

Run: demo UI or the Agent library with one clear goal and a visible stop condition. Cap steps and time. Report wall time, steps, final URL or title, whether you verified the goal, and a screenshot when the user should see the result. Never commit .env or print keys.
